title: One marked holding, one failed research run, and no recorded trade decision

One marked holding, one failed research run, and no recorded trade decision

Paper trading · 2026-11-03T17:00:54.593153-05:00

This report uses records through the fixed cutoff of 5:00:54 p.m. ET on November 3, 2026. The paper account snapshot was captured at that time; the MU valuation quote was observed at 4:52:04 p.m. ET. These are recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed, and the paper snapshot may precede fills. The supplied records contain one failed research run, but no completed day's trade decision, order proposal, deterministic risk approval or rejection, or broker fill. The mean-reversion book has a marked MU holding; the records do not show when it was filled. The other two books show $2,000 cash and equity each, with no supplied holdings.

Today's lesson: A marked price is not a fill

A midpoint is a bookkeeping estimate, not necessarily a price you could trade at. For MU, the recorded bid was $868.21 and ask was $1,138.13; their average is $1,003.17. Because those quotes are far apart, that midpoint is especially uncertain. It was observed at 4:52:04 p.m. ET, after the regular session, and is not a live price.

The snapshot may precede fills, as the context notes. No cutoff-date performance figure is supplied for the paper account; older performance records should not be read as today's result. What the records establish

The research run scheduled for 3:15 p.m. ET failed because the planner context exceeded its configured limit. The records do not include a completed book evaluation or an attempted decision from that run. No separate broker or simulated fill record is supplied, so the marked MU holding should not be treated as proof of a fill today.

What to watch next

Check whether a completed run, proposed order, deterministic risk result, and broker or simulated fill record appear in the next admitted records. Keep each stage distinct: a proposal is not an approval, an approval is not a fill, and a failed evaluation is not a decision.

Bid-ask midpoint: The average of the recorded bid and ask. It can be used to mark a holding, but it does not guarantee a trade at that price.

Unrealized gain or loss: The change in a holding's marked value compared with its purchase basis, before fees; it is not realized until a sale is recorded.

Deterministic risk check: A rule-based check that approves or rejects a proposed trade. No such result is included in today's supplied records.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
